By this order I shall dispose off the petition filed on behalf of the petitioner under Section 166 and 140 of Motor Vehicle Act for the death of the horse which was the only source of income of the petitioner.

In the present accident, SHO of PS Saket has also filed the DAR for the Road Traffic Accident occurred on 19.01.2015 at about 1.00 am at Press Enclave road, Opposite Select City Mall,
Saket, New Delhi wherein the animal i.e., Horse of the petitioner was died.

2. The facts of this case need not having any big canvas:-
"On 19.01.2015 at about 1.00 am, petitioner who was a horse cart owner was riding baggi and was returning from Karkardooma after attending marriage assignment.
When they reached Press Enclave Road, Opposite Saket City Mall, Saket along with his horse card was hit by a speeding truck bearing HR-55-L-2224.
Resulting to which horse received fatal injuries."
3. Notice of the petition was issued to the respondents.

This witness was put to the test of cross examination whereby he deposed that he was plying Baggi/ Horse Cart.
He deposed that when the accident was occurred, the offending vehicle hit to his horse from front left side in which three legs of his horse were fractured.
The truck driver was fled away from the spot along with truck.
The offending truck number is HR-55-L-2224.
He did not remember the colour of the offending truck.
The offending truck was full of mud.
He denied that the deceased belongs to Ras Breed.
He denied that he had not purchased the said horse for an amount of Rs. 3 lakh and filed a false receipt of the said amount.
He denied that Ex. PW 1/4 is a false photographs and not belongs to deceased horse.
He further admitted that he was having horse today and he has also such type of horse today also.
He has received Rs. 70,000/- in the criminal court for compounding the criminal case from the truck driver.
He admitted that the post moretm of the deceased horse was conducted and age of the horse is mentioned about seven years.
He denied that he was not earning Rs. 15,000/- per month.
He further denied that Rs. 50,000/- were not suffered in loss of love and affection.

sentences.text: In a petition under Motor Vehicles Act, Tribunal need not go into the technicality because strict rules of procedure and evidence are not followed.
Basically, in road accident cases, Tribunal has simply to quantify the compensation which is just rational and reasonable on the basis of enquiry.

Though it is an admitted legal position that the negligence on the part of driver with respect to the use of vehicle needs to be established but the same is to be established on the principles of preponderance of probabilities as decided in New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vs. Harsh Mishra & Ors. III(2015) ACC 435 Delhi.

Due to the death of the horse, he must have suffered at least three months loss of income.
Thus, the loss of income comes to 45,000/- (Rs. 15,000/- x 3).
I therefore award the petitioner the loss of income comes to Rs. 45,000/-.
15.Here in the present case, the petitioner has suffered loss of horse who died in the accident.

Petitioner has placed on record the original receipt Ex. PW 1/3 on record, however, he could not prove the said receipt as he would not bring the owner of the horse in the court from whom the petitioner had purchased the horse.
However, the horse who was died in the accident was of RAS BREED.
The value of such horses varies as per breed.
However, if we assume, the cost of the horse must be at least two - three lakh.
For this he has stated that in the post mortem report, the age of the horse has been shown as seven years.
Claimant has claimed that it was three years old.
However, it is a matter of fact that the horse was died and it has not been disputed by the insurance company that the horse was not died not died in the accident.
Irrespective of the age of the horse, at least there is some value of the horse.
As an average, a well dressed horse who is used in ceremonial function must be of at least Rs. 2 lakh.
Therefore, at least an amount of Rs. 2,00,000/- would be just Gulshan Kumar vs Parmanand Gupta And Ors.
